newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav army bank established - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav army bank established - agency.

text.p: The Yugoslav government and companies associated with the military have established an army bank, the state newsagency Tanjug reported on Friday.

The new institution, the Ju Garant Banka a.d., was created out of the military service of the Yugoslav National Bank (NBY), where a similar operation ran for 46 years, Tanjug quoted the army's information service as saying.

The bank will operate as an independent commercial bank from January 1 next year, with an initial credit potential of 760 million dinars ($152 million) of which its own founding capital stands at 216 million dinars, the statement said.

"Our bank... shall fully support the development and modernisation of the Yugoslav army and our military industry as well as the programmes of importance for the functioning of the federal state," said Vuk Obradovic the new director general who used to head the NBY's military service.

The bank's constituent assembly elected Yugoslav defence minister Pavle Bulatovic as its first president and finance minister Tomica Raicevic as chairman of the board of directors, at the recomendation of the federal government, the statement said.
